name: Ordering / Comparing Growth Rates of Multiple Functions
recognitionClueHinglish: Kai saare functions diye hain (mix of log, √n, n, n log n, n², 2^n, etc.) aur poocha hai 'increasing order of asymptotic growth rate' — ye is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (22 me se 7 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Classify each function into a known bucket FIRST (log-type, polynomial-type, exponential-type) — don't compare pairwise blindly.
Within the same bucket (e.g., two polynomials), compare exponents/leading terms directly.
Between buckets, the hierarchy is fixed: log < poly < exponential < factorial.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Sort functions into rough buckets: constant, logarithmic, polynomial (note the degree), exponential, factorial.
2. Order buckets using the fixed hierarchy.
3. Within any bucket with ties, apply the limit-ratio test f(n)/g(n) as n→∞ to break the tie precisely.
4. Double-check with a large concrete n (like n=1000) mentally if unsure, as a sanity check.
variationsObserved: Functions expressed as nested expressions (n^(log n), (log n)^n, n^√n) — apply logarithm to BOTH sides to compare exponent-type expressions cleanly.
commonTraps: Assuming a function 'looks bigger' (more terms/complex expression) without actually checking the dominant term.
Getting n^(log n) vs (log n)^n backwards — take log of both to compare log n · log n vs n · log(log n), the first grows faster.

name: TRUE/FALSE Verification of O/Ω/Θ Relationship Claims
recognitionClueHinglish: Do specific functions f(n), g(n) diye hain aur poocha hai 'f=O(g)?' ya 'f=Θ(g)?' TRUE hai ya FALSE, ya MULTIPLE such claims diye hain and asked which are correct — ye is topic ka doosra bada pattern hai (22 me se 9 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Apply the limit-ratio test f(n)/g(n) as n→∞ directly — fastest, most reliable method.
Remember O and Ω are NOT symmetric; only Θ is.
generalSolvingApproach: 2. If limit=0: f=o(g), so f=O(g) TRUE, f=Ω(g) FALSE. If limit=∞: reverse. If limit=positive constant: f=Θ(g), both O and Ω TRUE.
3. For multi-part claims (I, II, III...), evaluate each independently using the same test before picking the combined answer option.
variationsObserved: Functions defined via recurrences or summations rather than closed forms (need to solve/bound first, then compare).
Claims about a GENERAL property (true for ALL positive functions f) rather than one specific pair — needs a counterexample search, not just one ratio test.
commonTraps: Assuming f=O(g) ⟹ g=O(f) — false in general, only holds when f=Θ(g).
For 'true for all functions' claims, not searching hard enough for a counterexample before accepting a plausible-sounding claim.

name: Properties/Identities of Asymptotic Notation (transitivity, algebra, matching)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai ek GENERAL identity/property TRUE hai ya nahi (jaise transitivity, ya 'if f=O(g) with g replaced by...') — ye meta-level property pattern hai, specific functions ke bajaye notation ke rules test karta hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Transitivity holds for O, Ω, Θ individually.
Θ is symmetric; O and Ω are not.
Replacing g(n) by an equivalent/dominant expression preserves the O-relationship only if the replacement doesn't change the growth CLASS.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify which general rule the question is probing (transitivity, symmetry, substitution).
2. Verify against the known rule list rather than re-deriving from the epsilon-delta-style definition under time pressure.
3. If genuinely unsure, test with 2 concrete simple functions (like n and n²) to check the claimed property.
commonTraps: Assuming O behaves symmetrically like Θ.

name: Worst-case vs Average-case / Theoretical Lower Bounds
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai W(n) aur A(n) (worst/average case) ke beech relationship kya hai ALWAYS true hai, ya ek algorithm-class (jaise comparison-based sorting) ki theoretical lower bound poochi hai — ye theory-recall pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: W(n) ≥ A(n) ALWAYS (worst case can never be better than average) — this is the one guaranteed universal relationship.
Comparison-based sorting has a proven Ω(n log n) worst-case lower bound (decision-tree argument: n! leaf nodes, tree height ≥ log(n!) = Θ(n log n)).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For W(n) vs A(n) questions, the ONLY universally guaranteed relationship is W(n)≥A(n) — reject any option claiming a stronger or different universal relationship.
2. For sorting lower-bound questions, recall Ω(n log n) directly as a memorized fact rather than re-deriving the decision tree argument under time pressure.
variationsObserved: Recurrence-relation-defined function T(n), asked to classify its asymptotic behavior (bridges into the Recurrence Relation topic).
commonTraps: Assuming best-case, average-case, and worst-case have some fixed numeric ratio — no such universal ratio exists, only the ordering W≥A≥B holds.

name: Deriving Asymptotic Complexity from Pseudocode
recognitionClueHinglish: Pseudocode/function diya hai (loops ke saath) aur poocha hai iski asymptotic complexity kya hai, ya do code segments compare karne hain — ye derivation pattern hai, pehle CODE se complexity nikaalni hai, phir usko compare/classify karna hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Count loop iterations as a function of n first — is it linear, logarithmic (halving), quadratic (nested), etc.?
A while loop that repeatedly HALVES n runs O(log n) times; a for loop from 1 to n runs O(n) times; nested loops multiply their individual counts.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify each loop's iteration count as a function of the input size.
2. For nested loops, multiply; for sequential loops, add (and keep only the dominant term).
3. Once you have the derived complexity expression, apply the Ordering/TRUE-FALSE patterns above as needed.
commonTraps: Miscounting a halving-loop's iteration count as linear instead of logarithmic.
